findings.title: Docstring for `get_failure_reason` describes output the code never produces
findings.description: The docstring gives "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" as an example. The code actually builds that phrase with `get_text_list` and appends it to "check-ins detected", so the real output is "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected". The test at `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:310` asserts that real format. The docstring's "A failed check-in was detected" is also never returned. The singular branch uses `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP`, which yields "A missed check-in was detected", "An error check-in was detected", or "A timeout check-in was detected". The docstring also has the typo "humam readible". This text was moved verbatim from `mark_failed.py`, so the drift predates this change. The file is new, so it is the right time to fix it.

findings.title: Unused `logger` in the new modules
findings.description: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is defined in `incident_occurrence.py` and in `incidents.py:11`, and nothing calls `logger.` in either file. `mark_failed.py:11` also has an unused logger, which predates this change. Removing the unused logger and the `logging` import would clean this up.

findings.title: New modules have no dedicated tests, and some `get_failure_reason` branches are unasserted
findings.description: Coverage comes only through `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py`. The plural mixed-status message, the "An error check-in was detected" singular message, and the "8 timeout check-ins detected" message are asserted there. The singular "A missed check-in" and "A timeout check-in" messages are not. The "Never" fallback for `last_successful_checkin` is also not asserted anywhere under `tests/sentry/monitors`. This is test debt that existed before the move, not something this change introduced.

findings.title: Callers and test patch targets still resolve after the move
findings.description: `mark_failed` now delegates to `try_incident_threshold` with the same signature. The callers in `clock_tasks/check_missed.py`, `clock_tasks/check_timeout.py`, and `consumers/monitor_consumer.py` import only `mark_failed`, which is unchanged. A search of `src` and `tests` found no remaining references to `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, or `SimpleCheckIn` under `logic.mark_failed`. No `pyproject.toml` strict-typing override lists the affected modules. The `models.py` → `monitors/types.py` import direction introduces no cycle, since `types.py` does not import models.
